## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to apply fixed-width bit twiddling to real data without loops, a common pattern in systems programming.

## Key Concepts
- Byte masking with constants like 0x00FF00FF
- Cross-byte shifts (8 bits)
- Predictable, branch-free manipulation

## Code Example
```javascript
uint32_t swapAdjacentBytes32(uint32_t x) {
  return ((x & 0x00FF00FF) << 8) | ((x & 0xFF00FF00) >> 8);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend to 64-bit values? 
- What are performance trade-offs of this approach on different compilers?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests precise bit-mmask construction under edge-case shifts; no loops/branches is a common constraint in low-level systems.

## Key Concepts
- Bit masks and ranges
- Safe shifts with variable width (1..32)
- No branching; single expression mask composition

## Code Example
```javascript
uint32_t clearRange32(uint32_t x, unsigned a, unsigned b) {
  unsigned w = b - a + 1; // width of range
  uint32_t ones = (~0u) >> (32 - w); // w ones in LSBs
  uint32_t mask = ~(ones << a); // zeros in [a,b], ones elsewhere
  return x & mask;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to generalize to 64-bit with the same constraints?
- What if inputs are signed; does behavior change in C/C++?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assesses pattern recognition and solid bit-twiddling under time pressure.

## Key Concepts
- Alternating bit patterns (0101..., 1010...)
- Using XOR with shifted version to collapse pattern
- Detecting all-ones masks with (x & (x+1)) == 0

## Code Example
```javascript
function hasAlternatingBits(n) {
  const x = (n ^ (n >>> 1)) >>> 0;
  return (x & (x + 1)) === 0;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for 64-bit inputs?
- How to implement without using addition?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests constant-time bit manipulation skills, branchless thinking, and understanding of 64-bit mask patterns.

## Key Concepts
- **Pairwise masks**: `0x5...` (alternating `0101`) isolates even bits; `0xA...` (alternating `1010`) isolates odd bits
- **Complementary shifts**: left-shift even bits by 1, right-shift odd bits by 1, then OR combines them
- **No branching**: all operations are O(1) and branch-free

## Follow-up Questions
- **128-bit generalization**: process four 32-bit chunks in parallel using a vectorized approach, or extend the mask pattern
- **Performance verification**: benchmark against naive loop-based implementations to confirm O(1) constant-time behavior

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to manipulate multi-byte data with pure bitwise ops, a common low-level skill in performance-critical code.

## Key Concepts
- Byte masking with constants
- Shifts to relocate bytes
- Bitwise OR to assemble result
- No loops or branches; constant-time operation

## Code Example
```javascript
function swapBytes32(x) {
  return ((x & 0x000000FF) << 24) |
         ((x & 0x0000FF00) << 8)  |
         ((x & 0x00FF0000) >>> 8) |
         ((x & 0xFF000000) >>> 24);
}
```
